points: Subhash Kumar v. State of Bihar (1991): pollution-free water and air part of Art. 21.

PYQ-POL-WEB-554C25.lead: India has constitutional supremacy, not judicial supremacy.
points: Options 1-3 are true: the Constitution sets basic rules, defines powers, and is supreme law.

points: This is a Fundamental Duty in Part IVA.

Author

B.N. Rau was the Constitutional Adviser to the Constituent Assembly.

PYQ-POL-3570D718DFD1.lead: Free speech lets people question rulers — the core of democracy.
points: Democracy runs on open debate, criticism of government and free flow of ideas.
Equality before law and rule of law also exist in non-democratic states with good legal systems.
Freedom of worship is a religious freedom, not the defining mark of democracy.
PYQ-POL-3570D718DFD1.also: Article 19(1)(a) guarantees freedom of speech and expression in India.

PYQ-POL-3BEC7C3FCF3F.lead: The Executive carries out laws and runs day-to-day government.
points: Legislature makes laws.
Judiciary interprets laws and settles disputes.
NITI Aayog is a policy think tank, not a branch of government.

PYQ-POL-659357BD4F25.lead: Constitutional government means government whose powers are limited.
points: A constitution sets limits on what rulers can do and protects rights.
Popular, multi-party or legislature-led governments can still be unlimited.
Limits come through rights, separation of powers and judicial review.

PYQ-POL-6CDBE365A0CD.lead: Parens patriae: the State as guardian of those unable to protect themselves.
points: Latin for 'parent of the nation'.
State protects minors, persons of unsound mind and other helpless persons.
Option 2 describes repugnancy; option 3 relates to federal division; option 4 is judicial interpretation.
PYQ-POL-6CDBE365A0CD.also: Supreme Court applied it in Charan Lal Sahu v. Union of India (1990) on the Bhopal gas tragedy.

PYQ-POL-805E3CF1DF20.lead: Constitutionalism means limited power; despotism means unlimited, arbitrary power.
points: Despotism is rule by one person without legal limits.
Federalism and pluralism spread or share power, which fits constitutionalism.
Socialism is an economic ideology, not the opposite of limited government.

PYQ-POL-90CAF40678BB.lead: Audi alteram partem means 'hear the other side' — right to be heard.
points: It is one of the two main rules of natural justice.
The other rule, nemo judex in causa sua, is the rule against bias.
Reasonableness and free speech are separate legal ideas.
PYQ-POL-90CAF40678BB.also: Maneka Gandhi case (1978) read natural justice into Article 21.

PYQ-POL-9F7C6048D10E.lead: Democracy draws out the intelligence and character of ordinary people.
points: Democracy involves common citizens in public affairs, not just leaders.
Strong executives, single visionary leaders or party cadres are not its distinctive virtue.

PYQ-POL-A0049CBC7CEA.lead: Liberty means the opportunity to develop oneself fully.
points: This is the positive idea of liberty used by thinkers like Laski and T.H. Green.
Mere absence of restraint, or doing whatever one likes, leads to licence, not liberty.
Protection from tyranny is only one part of liberty.

PYQ-POL-B06E9B0825CA.lead: A State needs people, territory, government and sovereignty.
points: Option 1 covers all four elements, including independence from external control.
Option 2 misses territory and sovereignty.
Common language or culture (option 3) describes a nation, not a State.
Independent judiciary (option 4) is not an essential element.

PYQ-POL-B09D1B6C89A2.lead: Constitutional government is government limited by the constitution.
points: Being federal or representative does not by itself make a government limited.
Nominal or real head of state describes parliamentary vs presidential form, not constitutionalism.

PYQ-POL-D3BAEB7426E8.lead: Constitutionalism means the government's powers must be limited.
points: Having a constitution does not guarantee constitutionalism; dictatorships can have written constitutions.
Unlimited government and despotism are the opposite of constitutionalism.

PYQ-POL-D642EA085CBA.lead: 'Introduction to the Constitution of India' was written by D.D. Basu.
points: Durga Das Basu was a noted constitutional jurist; the book is a standard reference.
M.V. Pylee wrote 'India's Constitution' and 'Constitutional Government in India'.

PYQ-POL-DE0E2C074048.lead: A constitution's chief purpose is to define and limit government power.
points: It sets up offices, but its core aim is to restrain how power is used.
Law-making objectives and social justice are goals, not its chief purpose.

PYQ-POL-E18B3A693082.lead: Despotism — absolute, unchecked rule — is the opposite of constitutionalism.
points: Decentralisation, limited power and restraint of power all support constitutionalism.

PYQ-POL-EAA7A667FC02.lead: Reasonable laws protect liberty; they do not destroy it.
points: Liberty without law becomes licence where the strong dominate the weak.
More laws need not mean less liberty; it depends on whether laws are reasonable.
PYQ-POL-EAA7A667FC02.also: Article 19 allows only 'reasonable restrictions' on freedoms.

PYQ-POL-EB90B504ED58.lead: Separation of powers stops any one organ from becoming all-powerful.
points: Montesquieu argued liberty is lost when legislative, executive and judicial powers unite.
Centralisation of power threatens liberty.
Elected governments and judiciaries help, but work within the separation of powers.

PYQ-POL-F78D4EA5F73C.lead: Audi alteram partem means the right to be heard.
points: No one should be punished or decided against without a fair hearing.
Right to a lawyer and production before magistrate within 24 hours are Article 22 rights.

PYQ-POL-WEB-5033D2.lead: Upholding sovereignty, unity and integrity is a Fundamental Duty, Article 51A(c).

PYQ-POL-WEB-5033D2.also: Article 19(2) also allows restrictions in the interest of sovereignty and integrity of India.

PYQ-POL-0BC58F4CB541.lead: Constitutional government limits State power to protect individual liberty.

PYQ-POL-8586B30A8AAA.lead: A constitution gives basic rules that let diverse groups trust and cooperate.

It provides assurance: no group can be dominated or have its rights taken away.

PYQ-POL-A8B87FA08CBD.lead: Division of powers between Centre and units is essential to federalism.

Parliamentary supremacy fits unitary systems like Britain.
An Election Commission exists in unitary states too.

PYQ-POL-88F88F33F796.also: Nehru also chaired the Union Powers and States Committees; Patel the Provincial Constitution Committee.

PYQ-POL-9FE5E52E3A6C.lead: Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, 31 October, marks Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birth anniversary.
points: Observed since 2014; 2020 was his 145th birth anniversary (born 1875).
Nehru's birthday (14 Nov) is Children's Day; Indira Gandhi's death anniversary (31 Oct) is Rashtriya Sankalp Diwas.
PYQ-POL-9FE5E52E3A6C.also: Patel chaired the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal Areas.

PYQ-POL-A59B22BA37F4.lead: Sir B. N. Rau was the Constitutional Adviser to the Constituent Assembly.
points: He prepared the first draft (243 Articles, 13 Schedules) in October 1947.
Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar and K. M. Munshi were Drafting Committee members.
S. N. Mukherjee was the Chief Draftsman (printed as 'S. M. Mukherjee').
PYQ-POL-A59B22BA37F4.also: B. N. Rau later served as a judge of the International Court of Justice.

PYQ-POL-A609617BEF75.lead: The Constituent Assembly first met on 9 December 1946.
points: Dr Sachchidananda Sinha was the temporary President.
Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President on 11 December 1946.
The Muslim League boycotted the meeting; 211 members attended.

PYQ-POL-A698B56571A1.lead: Section 8(1) of the Indian Independence Act, 1947 recognised the Constituent Assembly.
points: Section 8(1) vested the Dominion legislature's powers in the Constituent Assembly, first for framing the constitution.
Section 8(2) kept the GoI Act, 1935 in force (adapted) until the Assembly made other provision.
Section 6 covered Dominion legislative powers; 10(1) and 4(2) are unrelated.

PYQ-POL-APK-288926.lead: The first meeting was held on 9 December 1946 in New Delhi.
points: It met in the Constitution Hall, now the Central Hall of Parliament.
26 January 1947, 9 December 1947 and 15 August 1948 are distractor dates.
PYQ-POL-APK-288926.also: H. C. Mukherjee and V. T. Krishnamachari were later elected Vice-Presidents.

PYQ-POL-APK-619DB5.lead: 2019 minus 1949 gives the 70th anniversary of adoption.
points: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949.
A joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament marked the 70th anniversary in 2019.

PYQ-POL-APK-7F4A49.lead: The Interim Government took office on 2 September 1946.
points: Jawaharlal Nehru was Vice-President of the Viceroy's Executive Council, acting as head.
The Muslim League joined on 26 October 1946.
It lasted until 15 August 1947.

PYQ-POL-APK-B11396.lead: Constitution Day is observed every year on 26 November.
points: It marks adoption of the Constitution on 26 November 1949.
2019 was its 70th anniversary.

PYQ-POL-APK-B37F40.lead: Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President on 11 December 1946.
points: Dr Sachchidananda Sinha was the temporary President.
H. C. Mookerjee was Vice-President; Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee; Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution.
PYQ-POL-APK-B37F40.also: Prasad later became India's first President (1950-62).

PYQ-POL-APK-D7D386.lead: 292 members were elected by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies.
points: Of 296 British India seats, 292 were for governor's provinces and 4 for chief commissioners' provinces.
The 93 princely state seats were to be filled by nomination by the rulers.
Elected members used the single transferable vote method.

PYQ-POL-APK-DCABAE.lead: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly.
points: Sachchidananda Sinha was the temporary President at the first meeting on 9 December 1946.
PYQ-POL-APK-DCABAE.also: H. C. Mookerjee and V. T. Krishnamachari were the two Vice-Presidents.

PYQ-POL-APK-DCE7A4.also: Nasiruddin called DPSPs 'like New Year resolutions broken on 2nd January'.

PYQ-POL-BA26183DB39C.lead: Constitution Day is right; the Drafting Committee date is wrong.
points: 26 November 1949 is the day the Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution.
Before 2015, 26 November was observed as National Law Day.

PYQ-POL-DA2C46EE0953.lead: The Assembly held 11 sessions, sitting on 165 days in all.
points: The Assembly worked for 2 years, 11 months and 18 days (Dec 1946 to Nov 1949).
Of the 165 sitting days, 114 days were spent on considering the Draft Constitution.
The other options give wrong session counts or day counts.
PYQ-POL-DA2C46EE0953.also: About 7,635 amendments were tabled; about 2,473 were actually discussed.

PYQ-POL-E01773A1DFEC.lead: Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar chaired the Credentials Committee.
points: Alladi was also one of the seven members of the Drafting Committee.

PYQ-POL-E13FC19EBEB4.lead: Seats followed population, not area; A and C are correct.
points: Members of each community were elected by that community's members in the provincial assembly.
Total strength was 389: 296 for British India, 93 for princely states.

PYQ-POL-E3863F530924.lead: Samvidhan Divas is 26 November, the day the Constitution was adopted (1949).
points: The Government began observing it as Constitution Day in 2015; earlier it was National Law Day.
26 January is Republic Day, when the Constitution came fully into force in 1950.
15 August is Independence Day; 18 November has no such link.

PYQ-POL-EB1048CC641B.lead: Section 8(1) gave the Constituent Assembly the power to frame the Dominion's constitution.
points: Section 8(1): the Dominion Legislature's power to make its constitution was to be exercised first by its Constituent Assembly.
The same clause made the Assembly the Dominion Legislature too, so it also acted as India's first Parliament.
Section 8(2) kept the Government of India Act, 1935 running until the new Constitution was made.
Sections 6, 10 and 4 deal with other matters (Dominion legislation, Secretary of State's services, Bengal/Punjab).

PYQ-POL-WEB-12D759.lead: The Constitution was adopted and enacted on 26 November 1949.
points: The Preamble says: 'adopt, enact and give to ourselves this Constitution' — dated 26 November 1949.
Some provisions (citizenship, elections, provisional Parliament) took effect that same day.
The rest came into force on 26 January 1950, Republic Day.

PYQ-POL-WEB-2E1B31.lead: Among the options, the earliest is the Swaraj Party's demand in 1934.
points: M. N. Roy first put forward the idea of a Constituent Assembly in 1934.
In 1934 the Swaraj Party (revived Swarajists) also demanded a Constituent Assembly.
Congress made it an official demand in 1935; the 1936 Faizpur session repeated it.
Muslim League 1942 and 1946 dates are far later.
PYQ-POL-WEB-2E1B31.also: The British accepted the demand in the August Offer of 1940.

PYQ-POL-WEB-3F5670.lead: The Draft Constitution was published in February 1948.
points: People were given about eight months to discuss it and suggest changes.
A second draft followed in October 1948 after these comments.
Ambedkar moved the Draft for consideration on 4 November 1948.

PYQ-POL-WEB-433F59.lead: Ambedkar called the Directive Principles a 'novel feature' of the Constitution.
points: He borrowed the idea from the Irish Constitution, as noted in the Assembly.
Ambedkar called Article 32, not DPSPs, the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.
The Preamble is often called the 'identity card' of the Constitution (N. A. Palkhivala).
PYQ-POL-WEB-433F59.also: Granville Austin called DPSPs and FRs together the 'conscience of the Constitution'.

PYQ-POL-WEB-45ADDD.lead: Ambedkar called Article 32, the Right to Constitutional Remedies, the heart and soul.
points: Article 32 lets a person go directly to the Supreme Court to enforce Fundamental Rights.
Without it, other rights would have no remedy, so Ambedkar valued it most.
The Right to Property was removed from Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment (1978).
PYQ-POL-WEB-45ADDD.also: The Supreme Court treats Article 32 as part of the basic structure.

PYQ-POL-WEB-52223D.lead: Members were indirectly elected by the provincial legislative assemblies.
points: In 1946, members of each community in a provincial assembly elected their own representatives.
Voting used proportional representation by single transferable vote.
Princely state members were to be nominated by their rulers, not by the British.
PYQ-POL-WEB-52223D.also: The Assembly was thus partly elected and partly nominated.

PYQ-POL-WEB-6330D4.lead: The first meeting was held in New Delhi on 9 December 1946.
points: It met in the Constitution Hall, now the Central Hall of old Parliament House.
The Muslim League boycotted it; 211 members attended.
PYQ-POL-WEB-6330D4.also: Sachchidananda Sinha presided as temporary President.

PYQ-POL-WEB-989010.lead: Communist member Somnath Lahiri called the Assembly British-made.
points: Lahiri said the Assembly was 'working the British plan as the British should like it'.
Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee and defended the Assembly's work.
B. N. Rau was the constitutional advisor, not a critic of this kind.

PYQ-POL-WEB-9C967B.lead: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946.
points: It was adopted unanimously on 22 January 1947.
Its modified form later became the Preamble.

PYQ-POL-WEB-A5B6F3.lead: The Cabinet Mission rejected the demand for a separate Pakistan.
points: The Mission (1946) proposed a weak Union with grouped provinces instead.

PYQ-POL-WEB-AA2141.lead: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the National Flag resolution on 22 July 1947.
points: The Assembly adopted the flag the same day, 22 July 1947.
The wheel at the centre is the Ashoka Chakra in navy blue.

PYQ-POL-WEB-BA5467.lead: Sir B. N. Rau was the Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly.
points: He prepared the first draft (October 1947) that the Drafting Committee worked on.
Ambedkar was Chairman of the Drafting Committee, not its advisor.
Sachchidananda Sinha was temporary President; B. Shiva Rao edited the Framing records.
PYQ-POL-WEB-BA5467.also: S. N. Mukherjee was the Chief Draftsman.

PYQ-POL-WEB-BDA322.lead: After Partition, Ambedkar was re-elected to the Assembly from Bombay.
points: In 1946 he was first elected from undivided Bengal (Jessore-Khulna seat).
That seat went to East Pakistan in 1947, so he lost his membership.
Bombay then elected him in July 1947, filling M. R. Jayakar's vacancy.
'West Bengal' did not exist in 1946, so option 1 is not apt.

PYQ-POL-WEB-C470A5.lead: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected President of the Assembly on 11 December 1946.

PYQ-POL-WEB-CCA155.lead: Nehru chaired the Union Constitution Committee.
points: Nehru also chaired the Union Powers and States Committees.
PYQ-POL-WEB-CCA155.also: Sardar Patel chaired the Provincial Constitution Committee.

PYQ-POL-WEB-D4D07D.lead: The Linguistic Provinces Commission was set up in 1948 under Justice S. K. Dhar.
points: It was appointed in June 1948 and reported in December 1948.
It favoured administrative convenience over language for reorganising states.
Justice Fazal Ali headed the States Reorganisation Commission of 1953.
PYQ-POL-WEB-D4D07D.also: The JVP Committee (Nehru, Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya, 1948) also rejected language as the basis.

PYQ-POL-WEB-E283C4.lead: H. V. Kamath compared the bulky Constitution to the elephant on the Assembly's seal.
points: Kamath said the bulkiest Constitution should fittingly resemble the elephant, the Assembly's crest.
Critics generally called it 'too long and too detailed'.
PYQ-POL-WEB-E283C4.also: Ivor Jennings called it 'too long and too rigid'.

PYQ-POL-WEB-E3BD0D.lead: The Assembly adopted Jana Gana Mana as National Anthem on 24 January 1950.
points: The National Song Vande Mataram was also adopted that day.
Rajendra Prasad was elected first President of India the same day.
It was the Assembly's last session day; members signed the Constitution then.

PYQ-POL-WEB-F06B7A.lead: Mahatma Gandhi was never a member of the Constituent Assembly or its Drafting Committee.
points: Other members: N. Gopalaswamy Ayyangar, Syed Mohammad Saadullah, N. Madhava Rau, T. T. Krishnamachari.
PYQ-POL-WEB-F06B7A.also: Madhava Rau replaced B. L. Mitter; T. T. Krishnamachari replaced D. P. Khaitan (died 1948).

PYQ-POL-WEB-F1525E.lead: The Drafting Committee was set up on 29 August 1947.
points: It had seven members, with B. R. Ambedkar as Chairman.
February 1948 is when it published the Draft Constitution.
15 August 1947 is Independence Day.

PYQ-POL-006127B7C80A.lead: India chose the parliamentary system, preferring responsibility to stability.
points: Ambedkar said a parliamentary executive faces daily checks through questions and no-confidence motions.
A presidential system gives more stability but checks responsibility only periodically.

PYQ-POL-045FBFD305E3.lead: After the RTE Act, the Centre brought the Right to Food law.
points: The RTE Act came into force on 1 April 2010.
The Right to Food took shape as the National Food Security Act, 2013.
No central Right to Health or Right to Shelter Act was enacted.
PYQ-POL-045FBFD305E3.also: NFSA covers up to 75% of rural and 50% of urban population.

PYQ-POL-0839800E7F53.lead: The Fifth Schedule governs Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.

Schedule

rows: Tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram

points: It provides Tribes Advisory Councils and gives the Governor power to make regulations.
PYQ-POL-0839800E7F53.also: Andhra Pradesh's agency areas are Fifth Schedule areas.

PYQ-POL-0AFA238C3891.lead: India is a federation with strong unitary features — 'quasi-federal'.
points: K. C. Wheare called the Indian Constitution 'quasi-federal'.
Federal features: two governments, division of powers, written rigid Constitution, independent judiciary.
Unitary features: strong Centre, single citizenship, Centre-appointed Governors, emergency powers.
Article 1 calls India a 'Union of States'.
PYQ-POL-0AFA238C3891.also: The Supreme Court in S. R. Bommai (1994) held federalism is part of the basic structure.

PYQ-POL-0E8A6D84ABDD.lead: The RPwD Act lists both under physical (locomotor) disability.
points: The Act lists 21 specified disabilities, up from 7 in the 1995 Act.
Locomotor disability also includes leprosy-cured persons and muscular dystrophy.
PYQ-POL-0E8A6D84ABDD.also: Benchmark disability means at least 40% of a specified disability.

PYQ-POL-1391296B0367.lead: Judicial review came from the USA, not Britain.
points: Britain follows parliamentary sovereignty, so its courts cannot strike down Acts of Parliament.

PYQ-POL-1C40A2C8A766.lead: Cri-MAC shares real-time information on heinous crimes, including human trafficking.

head: No.
Initiative
Purpose
rows: Delhi Police unit for women, children

points: Cri-MAC (Crime Multi-Agency Centre) was launched by MHA in 2020 on the CCTNS network.

PYQ-POL-204B1355B12D.lead: Article 343(1): Hindi in Devanagari script is the Union's official language.
points: Numerals are the international form of Indian numerals.
PYQ-POL-204B1355B12D.also: Official language provisions are in Part XVII (Articles 343-351).

PYQ-POL-210AD657AE47.lead: Residuary powers with the Centre were borrowed from Canada.
points: In India, Article 248 and Entry 97 of List I give residuary power to Parliament.
In the USA, residuary powers rest with the States.

PYQ-POL-30EE2F746FD5.lead: K. C. Wheare called the Indian Constitution 'quasi-federal'.
PYQ-POL-30EE2F746FD5.also: Ivor Jennings called it a 'federation with a strong centralising tendency'.

PYQ-POL-33614DB72AE6.lead: The Fifth Schedule deals with Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.
points: Ninth Schedule laws added after 24 April 1973 can be tested for basic structure (I. R. Coelho, 2007).
The Sixth Schedule covers Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram only.

PYQ-POL-3A08E7DA7346.lead: The Fifth Schedule covers Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.
points: The Tenth Schedule was added by the 52nd Amendment, 1985.

PYQ-POL-3B2BE5D006D9.lead: Each feature traces to a standard source country.
points: Option 3 pairs these features with their sources as per the full List-II.
PYQ-POL-3B2BE5D006D9.also: Ireland also gave nomination of Rajya Sabha members and the method of electing the President.

PYQ-POL-434D7FBC62C8.lead: Civil society helps by mobilising people and improving transparency.

True/False — why
rows: True — monitoring, RTI use, social audit
False — private gain, not public good

points: Civil society works for collective public interest, not profit.

PYQ-POL-43BA239A8758.lead: Governor, CAG and Emergency powers are centralising (unitary) features.

head: Item
Feature
Why it dents federalism
rows: Appointed by Centre, holds office at President's pleasure
One audit authority for Centre and States

points: All India Services (not Central Services) are the usual unitary feature, since they serve the States too.
PYQ-POL-43BA239A8758.also: Other unitary features: single Constitution, single citizenship, integrated judiciary, Art. 3 power over State boundaries.

PYQ-POL-45A462F26F5A.lead: 16 provisions, counting Art. 394 itself, came into force on 26 Nov 1949.
points: Article 394 says these and 'this article' commence at once — 16 in all.
The rest of the Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950.
PYQ-POL-45A462F26F5A.also: Many books list only the 15 Articles, leaving out Art. 394.

PYQ-POL-475C8DEA0217.lead: India follows the British-style parliamentary system at Centre and States.
points: President is the nominal head; real power lies with the Council of Ministers led by the PM (Art. 74).
Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (Art. 75(3)).
Not presidential: the executive depends on the legislature's confidence.
Not monarchical: the head of State is elected; 'unitary' is about Centre–State power, not form of government.
Today there are 12 Schedules.
9th added by 1st Amendment (1951); a 10th (Sikkim) added by 35th (1974) was repealed by 36th (1975); the present 10th (anti-defection) came by 52nd (1985).
11th Schedule (Panchayats) by 73rd and 12th (Municipalities) by 74th Amendment, 1992.
PYQ-POL-4881B75818FB.also: Original Constitution: Preamble, 395 Articles, 22 Parts, 8 Schedules.

PYQ-POL-4B7349BAE623.lead: CHAMPIONS is the MSME Ministry's single-window grievance and support portal.
PYQ-POL-4B7349BAE623.also: CHAMPIONS = Creation and Harmonious Application of Modern Processes for Increasing the Output and National Strength.

PYQ-POL-4E4F3498C221.lead: Cri-MAC shares crime information, including human trafficking, across agencies.
points: Cri-MAC = Crime Multi-Agency Centre, launched by MHA in 2020 under NCRB.
It shares alerts on heinous crimes and inter-state crimes nationwide in real time.
NDSO is the National Database on Sexual Offenders; ITSSO tracks investigation of sexual offences.

PYQ-POL-5D324E4E6586.lead: Part V (Articles 52–151) deals with the Union.
points: Chapter I of Part V (Arts. 52–78) covers the Union Executive: President, Vice-President, Council of Ministers, Attorney General.

PYQ-POL-764C5360837D.lead: All three benefits were provided under the Persons with Disabilities Act, 1995.
points: The 1995 Act was replaced by the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016.

PYQ-POL-77CFD9FE0C30.lead: UK–Rule of Law, Ireland–DPSP, USA–Judicial Review, Canada–Residual powers.
points: Option 2 links each country to its feature as per the full List-B.

PYQ-POL-7D8788522880.lead: Financial allocation tilts to the Centre; the other three are core federal features.
points: Independent judiciary settles Centre–State disputes (Art. 131).
Supremacy of a written Constitution binds both levels.
Distribution of powers via three Lists (Seventh Schedule) is the heart of federalism.
Resources are skewed toward the Centre, which hands grants to States — a unitary tilt.

PYQ-POL-85115707248A.lead: Seventh Schedule holds the Union, State and Concurrent Lists.

Schedule

points: Article 246 distributes law-making power through these Lists.
Residuary powers go to Parliament (Art. 248, Entry 97 of List I).

Provinces never sovereign; 1935 Act laid basis

points: Hence the Constitution calls India a 'Union of States' (Art. 1), not a federation.

PYQ-POL-8B13886E2AFF.lead: The Seventh Schedule has three Lists.
points: List I (Union), List II (State), List III (Concurrent).
Union law prevails in a Concurrent List clash, except as per Art. 254(2).
42nd Amendment (1976) moved five subjects, e.g. education and forests, from State to Concurrent List.
PYQ-POL-8B13886E2AFF.also: Concurrent List idea came from Australia.

PYQ-POL-8CB3DDC9A2A6.lead: India does not follow strict American-style separation of powers.
points: In a parliamentary system the executive sits in and answers to the legislature.
Quasi-federal is a known label (K.C. Wheare).
Fundamental Duties: Part IVA, Art. 51A (42nd Amendment, 1976).
DPSP: Part IV, Arts. 36–51.
PYQ-POL-8CB3DDC9A2A6.also: Art. 50 directs separation of the judiciary from the executive.

PYQ-POL-8EDA066FBD44.lead: Residuary powers with the Centre were borrowed from Canada.
points: Art. 248 and Entry 97 of List I give residuary powers to Parliament.
In the USA, residuary powers lie with the States.
South Africa: amendment procedure; Japan: 'procedure established by law'.

PYQ-POL-92C073898A55.lead: Inclusive development means growth that reaches every section of society.
points: Welfare schemes covering the poor, SCs, STs, women and minorities spread benefits widely.
Luxury projects, urban-only policies or big-industry-only growth leave many groups out.

PYQ-POL-982DEFF908C7.lead: Seema v. Ashwani Kumar (2006): SC ordered compulsory registration of marriages.

head: No.
Case
Known for
rows: Court can order medical test in divorce

PYQ-POL-9CBEB9E55901.lead: e-Kranti (NeGP 2.0) aims at electronic delivery of all government services.
points: e-Kranti was approved in 2015 as a pillar of Digital India.
e-Biz is a G2B business-services portal; the other two are not national missions of this kind.

PYQ-POL-A0EA677826CE.lead: 15 Articles came into force at once on 26 November 1949.
points: They cover citizenship, elections, provisional Parliament and transitional matters.
The remaining provisions began on 26 January 1950.
The Constitution was adopted on 26 Nov 1949 and came into force on 26 Jan 1950.
PYQ-POL-A0EA677826CE.also: Counting Article 394 itself, the figure becomes 16.

PYQ-POL-A35B79EF445C.lead: Union Judiciary is Chapter IV of Part V (Arts. 124–147).
PYQ-POL-A35B79EF445C.also: State High Courts: Chapter V of Part VI (Arts. 214–231).

False — NASSCOM with MeitY leads it

Article
Third Schedule oath
rows: Not an oath — Governor's ordinance power

PYQ-POL-APK-0059CA.also: Other Third Schedule Articles: 124(6) SC judges, 148(2) CAG, 164(3) State Ministers, 219 HC judges.

PYQ-POL-APK-075F80.lead: Article 47 directs the State to raise nutrition and standard of living.
points: Article 47 (DPSP): raise level of nutrition, standard of living and improve public health; prohibit intoxicating drinks.
Art. 24: no child labour in hazardous work; Art. 34: martial law; Art. 55: election of President.

PYQ-POL-APK-096FC8.lead: A UPSC member holds office for 6 years or until age 65.
points: Article 316(2) fixes the term: six years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
For State PSC members the age limit is 62.
PYQ-POL-APK-096FC8.also: UPSC members can be removed by the President on SC inquiry for misbehaviour (Art. 317).

PYQ-POL-APK-27339E.lead: The proviso to Article 164(1) requires a Tribal Welfare Minister in these States.
points: The 94th Amendment (2006) replaced Bihar with Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand; MP and Odisha remained.
Art. 163: Council of Ministers to aid Governor; Art. 162: State executive power; Art. 161: Governor's pardon.

PYQ-POL-APK-28F00D.lead: Social, economic and political justice came from the Russian Revolution (1917).
points: These ideals appear in the Preamble.
Liberty, equality, fraternity came from the French Revolution.
PYQ-POL-APK-28F00D.also: Russian (USSR) influence also gave Fundamental Duties.

PYQ-POL-APK-4591E0.lead: Article 335 balances SC/ST claims in services with administrative efficiency.
points: Art. 335 asks the State to consider SC/ST claims in Union and State posts, consistent with efficiency.
Art. 315: Public Service Commissions; Art. 325: single electoral roll; Art. 305: saving of existing laws on trade.
PYQ-POL-APK-4591E0.also: The 82nd Amendment (2000) added a proviso allowing relaxed marks for SC/ST in promotions.

PYQ-POL-APK-614246.lead: The eCourts Mission Mode Project began in 2007.
points: It came from the 'National Policy and Action Plan for ICT in Indian Judiciary', 2005, by the SC e-Committee.
Phase I ran from 2007; Phase III was approved in 2023.

PYQ-POL-APK-6841B7.lead: Article 46 protects educational and economic interests of SCs, STs and weaker sections.

PYQ-POL-APK-6D4CA4.lead: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act was passed in 2016.
points: It replaced the Persons with Disabilities Act, 1995.
It raised recognised disabilities from 7 to 21.
It gives 4% reservation in government jobs for persons with benchmark disabilities.
Art. 366(25) refers to tribes notified under Art. 342.
Art. 362: rights of former princely rulers (repealed); Art. 364: major ports and aerodromes; Art. 365: failure to comply with Union directions.
Art. 366(24) refers to castes notified under Art. 341.
Art. 363 bars courts in disputes from treaties with princely rulers; Arts. 362 and 364 are unrelated.
PYQ-POL-APK-7A1216.also: Article 366 is the definitions clause of the Constitution.

PYQ-POL-APK-93936F.lead: The First ARC was set up in January 1966.
points: It was first chaired by Morarji Desai, later by K. Hanumanthaiya.
It made 20 reports, including one on Centre–State relations (1969).
PYQ-POL-APK-93936F.also: Sarkaria Commission on Centre–State relations was set up in 1983.

PYQ-POL-APK-AEA48B.lead: The Second ARC (2005) was chaired by M. Veerappa Moily.
points: It submitted 15 reports, e.g. on RTI, ethics in governance and local governance.
Later chairpersonship passed to V. Ramachandran after Moily left in 2009.

PYQ-POL-APK-B9D5FE.lead: The Constitution adopted on 26 Nov 1949 had 395 Articles.
points: It also had a Preamble, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules.
Article numbering is still up to 395 though many Articles were added (e.g. 21A, 243A).
PYQ-POL-APK-B9D5FE.also: Today there are about 470 Articles in 25 Parts and 12 Schedules.

PYQ-POL-APK-BB9FCC.lead: The Eighth Schedule lists the scheduled languages, now 22.
points: Originally 14 languages; 92nd Amendment (2003) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali to reach 22.

PYQ-POL-APK-C78362.lead: Article 48 directs the State to prohibit slaughter of cows and calves.
points: Art. 48 covers organising agriculture and animal husbandry on scientific lines.

PYQ-POL-B629794CDF11.lead: India is federal in form but has strong unitary features.
points: Unitary features: strong Centre, single Constitution, emergency powers, Governors appointed by Centre.

PYQ-POL-B629794CDF11.also: The Supreme Court (S.R. Bommai, 1994) held federalism a basic feature.

PYQ-POL-B76F2C6AB4C3.lead: Seventh Schedule has three Lists: Union, State, Concurrent.

Residuary powers (Art 248) go to Parliament; they are not a separate List.
Originally 97, 66 and 47 entries.
PYQ-POL-B76F2C6AB4C3.also: Residuary powers to the Centre come from Canada.

PYQ-POL-BB6B474E56B8.lead: The First ARC was set up on 5 January 1966.

It gave 20 reports, including one recommending Lokpal and Lokayukta.
1947 and 1970 have no ARC link; 1856 is pre-Mutiny.
PYQ-POL-BB6B474E56B8.also: The Second ARC was set up in 2005.

True/False — why

False — Art 30 covers linguistic minorities too

Provision
Link to education
rows: Art 45 early childhood care; Art 46 weaker sections
Welfare of STs in Scheduled Areas
District Councils can run primary schools

points: The 42nd Amendment (1976) moved education from the State to the Concurrent List.

Schedule
Contents

Delhi Police unit for women and children

PYQ-POL-CFAE00F9470C.lead: The Fifth Schedule governs Scheduled Areas outside four Northeast States.

Art 244(2): those four States' tribal areas come under the Sixth Schedule.
Ninth Schedule shields laws from review; Seventh Schedule has the three Lists.
PYQ-POL-CFAE00F9470C.also: Other Northeast States like Manipur and Nagaland come under neither by name in Art 244(2).

PYQ-POL-D4B49C302327.lead: DPSP (Part IV) was borrowed from the Irish Constitution.
points: Ireland itself took the idea from the Spanish Constitution.

PYQ-POL-DD1DF0F1519E.lead: A federation needs an independent judiciary to settle Centre–State disputes.
points: In India, Art 131 gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction over such disputes.
Elected legislators and enforceable rights also exist in unitary states like the UK.
A regional-party minister is a coalition practice, not a structural feature.
PYQ-POL-DD1DF0F1519E.also: Other federal features: dual polity, written and rigid Constitution, bicameralism.

PYQ-POL-DD2A242ED111.lead: GeM (Government e-Marketplace) is the one-stop public procurement portal.
points: GeM was launched in August 2016 by the Commerce Ministry.
It replaced DGS&D for buying common-use goods and services.
e-Biz was a business-licence portal; e-Procure and GeP are not this marketplace.

PYQ-POL-DF9FF2456DD0.lead: AP Act 2 of 1998 set up the AP State Road Development Corporation.
points: APRDC develops and maintains core State roads and raises funds for them.
APSRTC dates from 1958 under the Road Transport Corporations Act, 1950.
Road Sector Project and Highway Development Project are programmes, not Act-created bodies.

PYQ-POL-DFFD1CA4C18D.lead: Tribal-majority regions notified for special protection are 'Scheduled Areas'.
points: Scheduled Areas are declared by the President under the Fifth Schedule.
'Forest only' and 'rural only' are too absolute; STs live in many settings.
STs are not mainly in metropolitan areas.
PYQ-POL-DFFD1CA4C18D.also: Sixth Schedule areas of the Northeast are called 'Tribal Areas'.

PYQ-POL-E70408F29CF7.lead: Indian federation was not made by an agreement among States.

head: No.
Feature
Indian federalism?
rows: No — 'Union of States', no right to secede

points: Ambedkar said India is indestructible; States can be reshaped by Parliament (Art 3).
The USA, by contrast, was formed by agreement and gives equal Senate seats.
The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.

PYQ-POL-E8D8F527A635.lead: Ambedkar said the Constitution can be both unitary and federal as needed.
points: He said it on 4 November 1948 while moving the Draft Constitution.
In an emergency, Parliament can legislate on State List matters (Art 250).
Paul Appleby called the system 'extremely federal'.

PYQ-POL-E92A1C55334B.lead: Cri-MAC gives police real-time information on heinous crimes, including trafficking.

head: No.
Initiative
Purpose

True — and it explains Statement I

PYQ-POL-F0DA2390EAEB.lead: The British could interfere to honour their international commitments.

Congress or popular requests were never a legal ground.
PYQ-POL-F0DA2390EAEB.also: Paramountcy lapsed under the Indian Independence Act, 1947.

PYQ-POL-F19628A9108E.lead: Scheduled Castes are popularly called Dalits today.

'Backwards' usually means OBCs.
PYQ-POL-F19628A9108E.also: 'Scheduled Castes' was first used in the Government of India Act, 1935.

PYQ-POL-F2062E0E2FE6.lead: Adult franchise gives every adult citizen the vote, subject to law.
points: Art 326: Lok Sabha and Assembly elections are on adult suffrage.
Voting age cut from 21 to 18 by the 61st Amendment, 1988.
A law can disqualify for unsound mind, crime or corrupt practice.

PYQ-POL-F63E2D6F5147.lead: The Government of India Act, 1935 is the biggest single source.

head: No.
Source
What it gave
rows: Federal scheme, Governor, PSCs, emergency, judiciary

points: About 250 provisions were taken from the 1935 Act, wholly or partly.
Art 395 repealed the 1935 Act and the Indian Independence Act, 1947.

PYQ-POL-F7DE0861C334.lead: The 2nd ARC backed damages from corrupt officials and whistleblower protection.
points: The 4th Report, 'Ethics in Governance', was submitted in January 2007.
PYQ-POL-F7DE0861C334.also: The 1st Report (2006) was on the Right to Information.

PYQ-POL-FF781653DBBA.lead: Scheduled Castes are commonly called Dalits.
points: 'Adivasis' are tribal people (Scheduled Tribes).
'Minorities' are religious or linguistic groups (Arts 29-30).
'Indigenous classes' is not a term for SCs.
PYQ-POL-FF781653DBBA.also: Art 341 lets the President notify the SC list for each State.

PYQ-POL-WEB-03617C.lead: Order: Sri Lanka (1931), Japan (1945), India (1950), USA (1965).
points: US women got the vote in 1920, but Black voters were blocked until 1965.

PYQ-POL-WEB-187E6D.lead: Leesamma Joseph (2021) upheld reservation in promotion for persons with disabilities.
points: The Supreme Court ruled on 28 June 2021.
It said disabled employees can get promotion quota even if recruited without it.
The case is linked to the Persons with Disabilities Act, 1995 and RPwD Act, 2016.

PYQ-POL-WEB-2620F8.lead: The Constitution sets up an independent, single integrated judiciary.
points: Security of tenure, fixed salaries and separation from executive (Art 50) protect judges.
India has no dual (federal + state) court system like the USA.
'Plural' and 'partial' are not constitutional descriptions.
PYQ-POL-WEB-2620F8.also: The Supreme Court is at the top; High Courts and subordinate courts below it.

PYQ-POL-WEB-2F4165.lead: The Union List covers national matters like defence and foreign affairs.
points: Only Parliament can make laws on Union List subjects.

PYQ-POL-WEB-2F580E.lead: The First Amendment, 1951 added the Ninth Schedule.
points: It protected land reform laws from challenge, along with Arts 31A and 31B.
I.R. Coelho (2007): post-24 April 1973 Ninth Schedule laws can be reviewed for basic structure.
The 42nd Amendment (1976) did not create any Schedule.

Clause
Subject

Claim (short)
True/False — why

PYQ-POL-WEB-39A25F.also: The Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950.

PYQ-POL-WEB-44365F.also: 71st Amendment (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali; 92nd (2003) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali.

PYQ-POL-WEB-51D9B4.lead: The Fourth Schedule allocates Rajya Sabha (Council of States) seats.

Subject

PYQ-POL-WEB-8017C7.lead: Independence of the judiciary is borrowed from the US Constitution.

PYQ-POL-WEB-89B39C.also: Tenth Schedule was added by the 52nd Amendment, 1985.

PYQ-POL-WEB-968646.lead: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission was set up in January 1953.

1947 is Independence; 1956 is States Reorganisation; 1959 matches no such commission.
PYQ-POL-WEB-968646.also: The Second Backward Classes Commission was the Mandal Commission (1979).

PYQ-POL-WEB-9A4983.lead: Maharashtra set up the first Lokayukta in 1971.

PYQ-POL-WEB-9A4983.also: The central Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act was passed in 2013.

PYQ-POL-WEB-A13881.lead: Reprieve stays, respite lessens, remission reduces, commutation substitutes.

PYQ-POL-WEB-A13881.also: President's pardoning power is Article 72; Governor's is Article 161.

PYQ-POL-WEB-AB79B2.lead: Being forced to be a witness against oneself is self-incrimination.

PYQ-POL-WEB-ACE09C.lead: Article 24 bans employing children below 14 in factories, mines and hazardous work.

Article 21A also gives free and compulsory education to children aged 6 to 14.

PYQ-POL-WEB-AF19E6.lead: India has a three-tier, single integrated judiciary.

PYQ-POL-WEB-BBA310.lead: This description of India is attributed to Carl Friedrich.
points: Carl J. Friedrich was a German-American political scientist who wrote on constitutional government.
Paul Appleby wrote reports on Indian public administration; Woodrow Wilson wrote on US administration.

PYQ-POL-WEB-BC780D.lead: India's law-making procedure follows the British parliamentary model.

PYQ-POL-WEB-C8CD1C.lead: The Fourth Schedule allocates seats in the Council of States.

PYQ-POL-WEB-D586E3.lead: The First Schedule lists States and Union Territories with their territories.

points: Parliament passes the main law and lets the executive frame rules, regulations and bye-laws under it.

PYQ-POL-WEB-E7AFE1.lead: Part III (Fundamental Rights) is called the Magna Carta of India.
points: Magna Carta (1215, England) was the first charter limiting the king's power.

points: Under Article 13, a law is void only to the extent it violates Fundamental Rights.
If the valid part can stand alone, courts retain it; the unconstitutional part is removed.
PYQ-POL-WEB-ECAAE8.also: Applied in A.K. Gopalan (1950) and R.M.D.C. v Union of India (1957).

PYQ-POL-WEB-ECFC89.lead: The Seventh Schedule has the Union, State and Concurrent Lists.
points: Elections are in Part XV; Emergency in Part XVIII; judiciary in Parts V and VI, not a Schedule.
Article 246 links these lists to law-making power.

PYQ-POL-WEB-F4A889.lead: Part IV, Articles 36–51, contains the Directive Principles.

PYQ-POL-00B238283058.lead: The Preamble lists liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith, worship, not occupation.
points: Options 1–3 are all Preamble words.
Freedom of occupation is a Fundamental Right under Article 19(1)(g), not a Preamble term.

PYQ-POL-0552C459727C.lead: 'We, the People of India' makes the people the source of power.
points: The Constitution is the supreme law, but its authority comes from the people.
Parliament and the President only use powers the Constitution gives them.

PYQ-POL-05AD4D0B9DAC.lead: The 42nd Amendment, 1976 added Socialist, Secular and Integrity.
PYQ-POL-05AD4D0B9DAC.also: These Preamble changes took effect on 3 January 1977.

PYQ-POL-06A24D04DD3F.lead: Sovereign means India is free of any external authority.
points: India is internally supreme and externally free; Commonwealth or UN membership does not change this.
'Republic' means an elected head of State; 'Democracy' means rule by elected representatives.

PYQ-POL-0772F84A4742.lead: Liberty, equality and fraternity come from the French Revolution (1789).
points: Social, economic and political justice is traced to the Russian Revolution (1917).
The idea of a Preamble itself comes from the US Constitution.

PYQ-POL-0FFFC5CEB131.lead: 'Freedom' is not a Preamble word; it is used for Articles 19–22.
points: The Preamble uses Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity.
Liberty and freedom mean the same in daily speech, but only 'Liberty' is in the text.

PYQ-POL-102E50C610E9.lead: The 42nd Amendment (1976) is the first and only Preamble amendment.
points: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held the Preamble is part of the Constitution and can be amended, but not its basic structure.

PYQ-POL-197ABDA34060.lead: The Preamble secures Justice: social, economic and political.

points: 'Democratic' and 'Republic' were in the original Preamble of 1950.

PYQ-POL-3104E71F71AC.lead: 'Sovereign' means India is not subject to any external authority.

PYQ-POL-42700D6908DD.lead: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 added 'Secular' to the Preamble.

Amendment
What it did

These ideals come from the French Revolution.

PYQ-POL-74237A505024.lead: Only one amendment, the 42nd (1976), has changed the Preamble.
points: It made three changes: added Socialist, Secular and Integrity.

PYQ-POL-74237A505024.also: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held the Preamble can be amended, but not its basic features.

PYQ-POL-768196C636E0.lead: 'Federal' is not in the Preamble; India is a 'Union of States'.

PYQ-POL-4586D0A72232.also: Fundamental Duties are in Part IVA (Article 51A).

PYQ-POL-46C2E6E50FCC.lead: Gopalan-detention, Maneka-liberty, Bommai-President's Rule, Indra Sawhney-reservations.
points: Correct code A-3, B-2, C-4, D-1 is option 2.
PYQ-POL-46C2E6E50FCC.also: Indra Sawhney fixed the 50% ceiling and the creamy-layer rule for OBCs.

PYQ-POL-46DE3AA93AC8.lead: Article 13(1) voids pre-Constitution laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights.

head: No.
Clause
Subject
rows: State cannot make laws abridging FRs

points: Article 13(1) is the basis of the doctrine of eclipse.

PYQ-POL-48DCE5CA42EA.lead: Fundamental Rights are justiciable and promote political democracy.

head: Stmt
Claim (short)
True/False — why
rows: False — from USA; DPSP from Ireland

PYQ-POL-48DCE5CA42EA.also: Directive Principles aim at social and economic democracy.

PYQ-POL-496F281D061D.lead: Property is no longer a Fundamental Right, so Article 32 is unavailable.

head: No.
Remedy
Available?
rows: Yes — High Courts protect legal rights

points: The 44th Amendment, 1978 removed Article 31 and made property a legal right under Article 300A.

PYQ-POL-4ADE4E1D118F.lead: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 came into force on 1 July 1961.
points: 20 May 1961 is the date of Presidential assent, not commencement.
1 June and 20 June 1961 are wrong dates.
It makes giving, taking or demanding dowry an offence.
Section 498A IPC (cruelty, 1983) and 304B IPC (dowry death, 1986) were added later.

PYQ-POL-4BB919732E3C.lead: Article 32 empowers the Supreme Court to issue writs.
points: High Courts under Article 226 can issue writs for FRs and 'any other purpose', so their writ power is wider.

PYQ-POL-4CF5E9089C42.lead: Article 20(2) gives protection against double jeopardy.
points: It applies only when a person was prosecuted and punished by a court for the same offence.
It does not apply to departmental or administrative proceedings.
The other three options are not legal terms for this protection.
PYQ-POL-4CF5E9089C42.also: Article 20(1) bars ex-post-facto criminal laws; 20(3) bars self-incrimination.

PYQ-POL-4D8A1F42157D.lead: Article 19 freedoms are available only to citizens.
points: Other citizen-only rights: Articles 15, 16, 29 and 30.
Correct code A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV is option 2.
PYQ-POL-4E2815A3CF9D.also: Article 18 exempts military and academic distinctions.

PYQ-POL-4F44363EBDEF.lead: Section 377 IPC criminalised consensual same-sex acts — an LGBT rights issue.
points: Suresh Kumar Koushal (2013) had upheld Section 377.
In 2016 the curative petitions were referred to a five-judge Bench.
Navtej Singh Johar (2018) decriminalised consensual adult same-sex conduct.
Free legal aid was read into Article 21 in M.H. Hoskot (1978) and Hussainara Khatoon (1979).
Article 22 (V) is the distractor: it gives right to consult a lawyer of choice on arrest.
PYQ-POL-5031979CD36B.also: Article 39A (42nd Amendment) directs the State to provide free legal aid.

PYQ-POL-50E26166E9DB.lead: Freedom of speech (Article 19(1)(a)) is for citizens only.
points: Articles 15 and 16 in the equality group are citizen-only, but Article 14 covers everyone.

PYQ-POL-52C20F13D4FF.lead: Article 16(4A) is about SC/ST reservation in promotions.
points: The 85th Amendment, 2001 added consequential seniority.
M. Nagaraj (2006) upheld these amendments with conditions.

PYQ-POL-53D2661F2CCE.lead: Article 20(1) bars retrospective criminal laws, so statement 2 is wrong.

head: No.
Claim (short)
True/False — why
rows: Parliament can make retrospective criminal law
No compulsion to be witness against self
Art 22 safeguards not for preventive detainees

points: Civil and tax laws can be retrospective; only criminal laws cannot.

PYQ-POL-557A42B74133.lead: Foreigners get Article 14 equality and Article 21 life and liberty.
points: Foreigners also get Articles 20, 22 (not enemy aliens), 23-24 and 25-28.

PYQ-POL-578614405D30.lead: Code a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i matches first chairpersons.
points: NCSC and NCST became separate bodies after the 89th Amendment, 2003.
NCBC got constitutional status under Article 338B by the 102nd Amendment, 2018.

PYQ-POL-591B828C49BC.lead: Under Article 32 a person goes directly to the Supreme Court: original jurisdiction.
points: Unlike Article 131, the Article 32 remedy is itself a Fundamental Right.

PYQ-POL-5CD185446D85.lead: Article 34 is about martial law, not SC economic safeguards.

head: No.
Article
Subject
rows: Promote economic, educational interests of SC/ST
Ban on forced labour and begar

points: Articles 23, 24 and 46 are listed as economic safeguards for Scheduled Castes.

PYQ-POL-5D10D5888283.lead: Article 12 does not mention courts, so their status as 'State' is unclear.
points: Courts acting judicially are not 'State' (Naresh Shridhar Mirajkar, 1966).
Their administrative or rule-making acts can be tested against Part III.
Municipal corporations and panchayats are clearly 'local authorities'.

PYQ-POL-602F300F9B4D.lead: The 1995 Act reserved at least 3% of vacancies for persons with disabilities.
points: Section 33: 1% each for blindness/low vision, hearing impairment and locomotor disability.
Reservation was computed on total vacancies in a cadre (Union of India v. National Federation of the Blind, 2013).
The 2016 RPwD Act raised it to 4%.

PYQ-POL-625DA8B76F85.lead: Article 23 bans begar and forced labour, which covers bonded labour.

head: No.
Article
Subject
rows: Ban on begar, forced labour, trafficking
Ban on child labour in factories/mines

points: The exact definition of 'bonded labour' is in the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976, made to enforce Article 23.
PYQ-POL-625DA8B76F85.also: Articles 23 and 24 together form the Right against Exploitation.

PYQ-POL-6315A0E8AFC1.lead: Quo warranto asks a person by what authority he holds a public office.

head: No.
Purpose
Writ
rows: Question right to hold public office

points: Quo warranto lies only for a substantive public office created by statute or Constitution.
Any person can seek it, not only an aggrieved person.

PYQ-POL-637427A1131A.lead: Certiorari makes a lower court send its case records to a higher court.

head: No.
Purpose
Writ
rows: Move case between any two courts

points: The higher court then quashes the order if passed without jurisdiction or with an error of law.
Certiorari is curative (after the order); prohibition is preventive (before it).

PYQ-POL-65736CB2BA39.lead: Only B and C state the standard textbook rules on writs.

head: Stmt
Claim (short)
True/False — why
rows: Habeas corpus only against public authorities

points: So the answer is B and C only.
PYQ-POL-65736CB2BA39.also: Mandamus also cannot be issued against the President or State Governors.

PYQ-POL-65EED9CE550B.lead: Habeas corpus orders the detained person's body to be produced before court.
points: Habeas corpus means 'to have the body'.
It can be issued against both public authorities and private persons.

PYQ-POL-6675D5C10A80.lead: The Constitution neither defines basic structure nor expressly mentions 'judicial review'.

head: Stmt
Claim (short)
True/False — why
rows: False — doctrine made by Supreme Court
False — not expressly stated; implied power

points: Basic structure came from Kesavananda Bharati (1973); its parts are listed by courts case by case.
Judicial review flows from Articles 13, 32 and 226, but the term is not in the text.
PYQ-POL-6675D5C10A80.also: Judicial review itself is part of the basic structure (Minerva Mills 1980, L. Chandra Kumar 1997).

PYQ-POL-66B995530AFB.lead: Article 300A makes property a legal right available to every person.

head: No.
Option
Why right/wrong
rows: Wrong — removed from Part III in 1978
Wrong — it is a constitutional/legal right

points: The 44th Amendment, 1978 omitted Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 and inserted Article 300A in Part XII.
For its violation, one goes to the High Court under Article 226, not Article 32.

PYQ-POL-66C7102B892D.lead: Article 20 protects against ex post facto laws, double jeopardy and self-incrimination.
points: Art 20(1): no retrospective criminal law; 20(2): no double punishment; 20(3): no self-incrimination.
PYQ-POL-66C7102B892D.also: Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency (44th Amendment).

PYQ-POL-672CA7F1D7E2.lead: Laws in the Ninth Schedule were shielded from challenge on Fundamental Rights.
points: The 76th Amendment Act, 1994 put Tamil Nadu's 69% reservation law in the Ninth Schedule.
Ninth Schedule was added by the 1st Amendment, 1951 (Article 31B).
PYQ-POL-672CA7F1D7E2.also: I.R. Coelho (2007): laws added after 24 April 1973 can be reviewed for basic structure.

PYQ-POL-6A5483A2C9C6.lead: Article 18 allows only military or academic distinctions to be conferred.
points: Article 18(1): 'No title, not being a military or academic distinction, shall be conferred by the State.'
Royal and hereditary titles are exactly what Article 18 abolishes, so options 3 and 4 are wrong.
There is no 'constitutional title' exception (option 1).
PYQ-POL-6A5483A2C9C6.also: Balaji Raghavan (1995): Bharat Ratna and Padma awards are not titles, but cannot be used as prefixes/suffixes.

PYQ-POL-6C7609D2C14F.lead: Article 24 bans employing children below 14 in factories, mines, hazardous work.
PYQ-POL-6C7609D2C14F.also: Articles 23 and 24 form the Right against Exploitation.

PYQ-POL-6F5D85D4F73A.lead: Not punishing twice for one offence is the doctrine of double jeopardy.
points: Article 20(2) protects only after prosecution and punishment by a court; departmental action does not count (Maqbool Hussain, 1953).

PYQ-POL-76E6F1F61DC1.lead: The Court upheld criminal defamation, IPC Sections 499 and 500.
points: Subramanian Swamy v. Union of India was decided in May 2016.
Defamation is an express ground of restriction in Article 19(2).
The Court treated reputation as part of the right to life under Article 21.
Sedition, blasphemy and obscenity were not the provisions in issue.

PYQ-POL-77C9941B15EC.lead: Part III order: Equality, Freedom, Religion, Cultural-Educational, Constitutional Remedies.
points: Right against Exploitation (23–24) comes between Freedom and Religion but is not listed here.
So the sequence is D, C, B, E, A — option 2.

PYQ-POL-7A33BDAF645D.lead: Mandamus commands a public authority to perform its public duty.
points: Mandamus means 'we command'.
It does not lie against a private individual or private body (options 3, 4), except where a public duty is involved.
It can also go to lower courts, but the standard answer is public authority.
PYQ-POL-7A33BDAF645D.also: Mandamus cannot be issued against the President or State Governors.

PYQ-POL-7AADD9E03E00.lead: Privacy is part of life and personal liberty under Article 21.

head: No.
Article
Subject
rows: No discrimination on religion, caste, sex etc.
Life and personal liberty incl. privacy

points: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (24 August 2017): nine-judge bench, unanimous.
It overruled M.P. Sharma (1954) and Kharak Singh (1962) on this point.
PYQ-POL-7AADD9E03E00.also: Privacy is not absolute; limits must pass legality, legitimate aim and proportionality.

PYQ-POL-7C5FA5C4A067.lead: A.K. Gopalan (1950) read 'procedure established by law' narrowly.
points: Gopalan held any procedure in a valid law is enough; no American 'due process'.
Maneka Gandhi (1978) changed this: procedure must be fair, just and reasonable.

PYQ-POL-7CAB9C8D5D22.lead: The Right to Education Act was passed in 2009.
points: Full name: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009.
It came into force on 1 April 2010 — option 4 is the commencement year, not passing year.
It gives effect to Article 21A (children aged 6 to 14).
PYQ-POL-7CAB9C8D5D22.also: Article 21A was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

PYQ-POL-7CB608E7C4E9.lead: Quo warranto literally means 'by what authority' or 'by what warrant'.
points: The court asks the office holder to show the legal authority for holding a public office.
Options 2–4 describe kinds of authority, not the meaning of the words.
PYQ-POL-7CB608E7C4E9.also: Quo warranto lies only for a substantive public office, not a private or ministerial post.

PYQ-POL-7CC62124D2A3.lead: Free and compulsory education (6–14 years) is a Fundamental Right, Article 21A.

head: No.
Option
Status
rows: Enabling provision Art 16(4A), not a right
Art 24 — only factories, mines, hazardous work
Part of Art 19(1)(a) by court ruling

points: Article 21A was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002; the RTE Act followed in 2009.

PYQ-POL-803B19401388.lead: Gujarat was the first State to implement 10% EWS reservation, January 2019.
points: Gujarat applied the EWS quota from 14 January 2019, the day the central rule came into force.
The quota comes from the 103rd Amendment Act, 2019 (Articles 15(6) and 16(6)).

PYQ-POL-8230CB1C5972.lead: The 103rd Amendment allows up to 10% reservation for economically weaker sections.
points: Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (7 November 2022) upheld it by a 3:2 majority.
The quota covers education (Article 15(6)) and public jobs (Article 16(6)).
The Court held economic criteria alone can be a basis for reservation.
PYQ-POL-8230CB1C5972.also: EWS quota excludes SC, ST and OBC, and is over and above existing reservations.

PYQ-POL-82ACA523DBB8.lead: Freedom of Religion is in Articles 25 to 28.
points: Art 25: conscience and religion; 26: manage religious affairs; 27: no tax for a religion; 28: religious instruction in institutions.

PYQ-POL-865AF9CCE260.lead: Article 32 lets a person move the Supreme Court directly to enforce Fundamental Rights.

head: No.
Article
Subject
rows: Parliament may limit FRs of armed forces

points: Ambedkar called Article 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

PYQ-POL-875B90704E4F.lead: Mandamus is Latin for 'we command' — an order to perform a public duty.

head: No.
Word
Linked to
rows: A ground for review, not a meaning

PYQ-POL-8AC08B562241.lead: After RTE, the Centre brought the National Food Security (Right to Food) Bill.
points: The National Food Security Bill was introduced in Lok Sabha in December 2011.
It became the National Food Security Act, 2013.
No central Right to Health or Right to Shelter Act was introduced then.

PYQ-POL-8AC23F763FF4.lead: Article 12 defines 'the State' for Part III.
points: It includes Union and State governments and legislatures, and all local or other authorities.
PYQ-POL-8AC23F763FF4.also: Courts treat bodies that are instrumentalities of government as 'other authorities' (Ajay Hasia, 1981).

PYQ-POL-8B4A831221B2.lead: Right to Property is no longer a Fundamental Right since 1978.
points: The 44th Amendment, 1978 removed Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 and added Article 300A.

PYQ-POL-8C7C3EB46579.lead: Article 14 forbids class legislation but allows reasonable classification.
points: Class legislation means arbitrarily picking a group for special favour or burden.
Classification is valid if it has an intelligible differentia and a rational link to the law's object.
Protective and differential laws (e.g., for women, children, backward classes) are allowed if they pass this test.

PYQ-POL-8DB488C52D02.lead: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 came into force on 1 July 1961.
points: It was passed on 20 May 1961 (assent date), which is option 1 — a common trap.
It applies to the whole of India.
PYQ-POL-8DB488C52D02.also: Section 498A IPC (cruelty) and 304B IPC (dowry death) were added in 1983 and 1986.

PYQ-POL-9106AE56F56D.lead: Article 12's wide wording plus many court rulings make 'State' hard to pin down.
points: The definition is inclusive ('includes'), and 'other authorities' is not defined.
Courts have widened it case by case (Rajasthan SEB 1967, Ajay Hasia 1981, Pradeep Kumar Biswas 2002).
Whether a body is State often depends on government control and funding, a policy-type judgement.

PYQ-POL-92E39634C4DF.lead: Double jeopardy is in Article 20(2), part of the Right to Freedom (19–22).

PYQ-POL-946A6A8050FA.lead: Article 19(1) now guarantees six freedoms to citizens.
points: They are: speech, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession/trade.
Originally seven; property (19(1)(f)) was omitted by the 44th Amendment, 1978.
Each freedom is subject to reasonable restrictions under clauses (2) to (6).
PYQ-POL-946A6A8050FA.also: Article 19 rights are available only to citizens, not foreigners.

PYQ-POL-95E6B449F9B7.lead: Habeas corpus lies against private persons too, so statement 3 is false.

head: No.
Statement
Correct?
rows: Not if detention outside court's jurisdiction

points: Habeas corpus is also refused where detention is by a court order or for contempt of court/legislature.

PYQ-POL-95F0CB851860.lead: Begar means forced work taken without any payment.
points: Article 23(1) bans begar, human trafficking and other forced labour.
Voluntary unpaid work (option 1) is not begar, since there is no force.
Paying below minimum wage can be 'forced labour' (PUDR, 1982), but that is not begar.
PYQ-POL-95F0CB851860.also: Article 23(2) allows compulsory public service, like military service, without discrimination.

PYQ-POL-969C87171A34.lead: Article 32 is the Right to Constitutional Remedies.
points: It lets a person go straight to the Supreme Court, which can issue the five writs.
PYQ-POL-969C87171A34.also: Ambedkar called Article 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

PYQ-POL-96A3ADFBE4E6.lead: Article 16(3) lets Parliament prescribe residence for certain public jobs.

head: No.
Article
Subject
rows: No tax to promote a religion

points: Article 16(2) bans job discrimination on residence; 16(3) is the exception.
Only Parliament, not State legislatures, can make this law (Article 35).
PYQ-POL-96A3ADFBE4E6.also: Parliament used it in the Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act, 1957.

PYQ-POL-97244FD83A3D.lead: The Central Government notifies minorities under the NCM Act, 1992.
points: The Constitution uses 'minority' (Articles 29, 30) but does not define it.
Section 2(c) of the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992 lets the Centre notify minority communities.
Six are notified: Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains.
PYQ-POL-97244FD83A3D.also: Jains were added as a notified minority in 2014.

PYQ-POL-97612B70243E.lead: Both are right: no unqualified right to marry; travel abroad is within Article 21.

head: Stmt
Claim (short)
True/False — why
rows: Travel abroad is a Fundamental Right

points: Choice of partner is still protected under Article 21 (Shafin Jahan, 2018); A means no right to State-recognised marriage.

PYQ-POL-981259F90754.lead: Article 13(2) bars the State from making laws that abridge Fundamental Rights.
points: Any law breaking this is void to the extent of the conflict.
Article 13 has only four clauses, so 13(5) and 13(7) do not exist.
Article 13(4), added by the 24th Amendment (1971), excludes constitutional amendments from Article 13.
PYQ-POL-981259F90754.also: Article 13(1) covers pre-Constitution laws and is the basis of the doctrine of eclipse.

PYQ-POL-988E531C62A2.lead: Article 20(2) bars prosecuting and punishing anyone twice for one offence.

head: No.
Article
Deals with
rows: Double jeopardy, ex post facto, self-incrimination

points: Protection applies only after prosecution and punishment by a court or judicial tribunal.
It does not bar departmental or administrative proceedings for the same act.
PYQ-POL-988E531C62A2.also: Article 20 has three parts: 20(1) ex post facto, 20(2) double jeopardy, 20(3) self-incrimination.

PYQ-POL-98966D9E30B3.lead: Article 13(2) forbids laws that take away or abridge Part III rights.
points: Exact words: the State shall not make any law which 'takes away or abridges' the rights in Part III.
Option 1 (abridges) is also part of the text; 'takes away' is the first verb used.
Part IV holds Directive Principles; Article 13 does not protect them.
A law violating this is void to the extent of the conflict.
PYQ-POL-98966D9E30B3.also: Article 13(4), added by the 24th Amendment (1971), excludes constitutional amendments from 'law' under Article 13.

PYQ-POL-9949445CFC8B.lead: Article 21A gives free and compulsory education to children aged 6–14.
points: 21A was inserted by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.
The RTE Act, 2009 gives effect to it; both came into force on 1 April 2010.
Earlier, courts read education into Article 21 (Mohini Jain 1992, Unni Krishnan 1993).
PYQ-POL-9949445CFC8B.also: The same 86th Amendment changed Article 45 (DPSP) and added duty 51A(k) for parents.

PYQ-POL-9B2341745553.lead: Most rights bind the State, but some also bind private individuals.
points: Articles 15(2), 17, 23 and 24 can be enforced against private persons too.
So rights can be claimed against both the State and private individuals.
Option 3 (only State) misses these rights; options 1 and 4 ignore the State.
Most Part III rights, like Article 14 or 19, apply only against the 'State' under Article 12.
PYQ-POL-9B2341745553.also: Article 12 defines 'State' to include Union, States, local and other authorities.

PYQ-POL-9BABB167A5F8.lead: The 44th Amendment, 1978 removed property from the Fundamental Rights.
points: The amendment omitted Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31.
Property is now a constitutional (legal) right under Article 300A in Part XII.

PYQ-POL-9C662F5674C8.lead: The Supreme Court held choice of life partner is part of Article 21.
points: Shafin Jahan v. Asokan K.M. (Hadiya case, 2018) linked marriage choice to Article 21.
Shakti Vahini v. Union of India (2018) protected couples from khap panchayat threats.
PYQ-POL-9C662F5674C8.also: Supriyo Chakraborty (2023) said there is no unqualified fundamental right to marry as an institution.

PYQ-POL-9D42C1CB0887.lead: High Courts issue writs under Article 226.

head: No.
Article
Deals with
rows: Parliament's power on certain Part III laws
HC withdraws case from lower court

points: Article 226 covers Fundamental Rights 'and for any other purpose', so it is wider than Article 32.
Article 32 is limited to enforcing Fundamental Rights.
PYQ-POL-9D42C1CB0887.also: Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right; Article 226 is not.

PYQ-POL-9DF21ADDBAFB.lead: Under Article 32, a person can directly approach the Supreme Court.
points: No need to go to a High Court first for a Fundamental Rights violation.
Article 131 is also original jurisdiction, but only for federal disputes.
PYQ-POL-9DF21ADDBAFB.also: Ambedkar called Article 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

PYQ-POL-A1BEDB62082E.lead: The 44th Amendment, 1978 deleted the right to property from Part III.
points: It omitted Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31, effective 20 June 1979.
Property became a legal right under the new Article 300A.
Right to Freedom and Right to Equality still remain Fundamental Rights.
Right to Education was added, not removed, by the 86th Amendment, 2002.
PYQ-POL-A1BEDB62082E.also: The 44th Amendment also said Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended during an Emergency.

PYQ-POL-A22F2BB410B6.lead: Ex post facto law means a law that acts retrospectively.
points: It applies to acts done before the law was made.
Article 20(1) bars retrospective criminal laws and higher punishment than at the time of the act.
Retrospective civil and tax laws are not barred by Article 20(1).
Earlier, present and future law do not describe this backward effect.

PYQ-POL-A3C464F8CBC6.lead: K.A. Najeeb (2021) linked bail after long undertrial custody to Article 21.
points: A three-judge Bench upheld bail for an accused jailed over five years under UAPA without trial.
The Court said Section 43-D(5) UAPA cannot override the right to speedy trial under Article 21.
Articles 14, 16 and 19 (equality, public jobs, freedoms) were not the basis.
PYQ-POL-A3C464F8CBC6.also: Speedy trial was first read into Article 21 in Hussainara Khatoon (1979).

PYQ-POL-A4CD0991F7E0.lead: Legislatures, not the Supreme Court, impose limits on Fundamental Rights.
points: The question asks for the incorrect statement, so statement 1 is the answer.
Courts only test whether restrictions made by law are reasonable.

PYQ-POL-A7629A72C272.lead: An ex post facto law, by definition, operates retrospectively.
points: It reaches back to acts done before the law was passed.
Article 20(1) forbids such laws only for creating crimes or raising penalties.
Prospective or future laws apply only from now on — the opposite idea.
A proposed Bill is not yet a law at all.

PYQ-POL-A792422D688A.lead: The Court treated maternity benefit as part of the right to life (Article 21).
points: K. Umadevi v. Government of Tamil Nadu (2025) linked maternity benefit to reproductive rights and dignity.
Her two earlier children were born before she joined service, from a first marriage.
Articles 14, 23 and 21A deal with equality, exploitation and education — not the main basis.
PYQ-POL-A792422D688A.also: Reproductive choice was earlier read into Article 21 in Suchita Srivastava (2009).

PYQ-POL-A9151258E624.lead: Each writ's Latin name gives its meaning.
points: So the correct code is option 2 (a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i).
Option 1 repeats 'iv' for two items, so it cannot be right.
PYQ-POL-A9151258E624.also: Prohibition means 'to forbid'; it is issued before a lower court decides.

PYQ-POL-A984908A3FA4.lead: Article 33 lets Parliament restrict Fundamental Rights of the armed forces.
points: It covers armed forces, paramilitary, police, intelligence bodies and similar.
Only Parliament, not State legislatures, can make such laws.
PYQ-POL-A984908A3FA4.also: Article 34 restricts rights while martial law is in force.

PYQ-POL-AABBDB75971B.lead: Article 15(3) allows special provisions for women and children.

head: No.
Clause
Provides
rows: Special provisions for SEBC, SC, ST

points: 15(4) was added by the 1st Amendment, 1951; 15(5) by the 93rd Amendment, 2005.
PYQ-POL-AABBDB75971B.also: 15(6), added by the 103rd Amendment (2019), enables EWS provisions.

PYQ-POL-AC92B26EA0EF.lead: Articles 14 to 18 form the Right to Equality.
points: 14 equality before law; 15 no discrimination; 16 equal job opportunity; 17 untouchability; 18 titles.
PYQ-POL-AC92B26EA0EF.also: Six groups start at Articles 14, 19, 23, 25, 29 and 32.

PYQ-POL-AC9E5D3B17F3.lead: Article 24 bans employing children below 14 in factories, mines, hazardous work.
points: The Child Labour Act, 1986 (amended 2016) gives it legal force.

PYQ-POL-AD208C7C6B4D.lead: Press freedom is part of free speech under Article 19(1)(a).
points: The Constitution does not mention the press separately.
Romesh Thappar (1950) and Indian Express (1985) read it into 19(1)(a).
It is subject to reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2).

PYQ-POL-APK-04B6F0.lead: Article 14 guarantees equality before law and equal protection of laws.
points: It applies to 'any person', citizens and foreigners alike.
PYQ-POL-APK-04B6F0.also: 'Equality before law' is from Britain; 'equal protection of laws' from the USA.

PYQ-POL-APK-158179.lead: Mandamus ('we command') orders an authority to do its legal duty.

head: No.
Writ

PYQ-POL-APK-4360E4.lead: Article 112: Annual Financial Statement shows estimated receipts and expenditure for the year.

PYQ-POL-APK-4A8AB6.lead: Only the President can pardon sentences given by a court martial.

The Governor (Article 161) has no power over court-martial sentences.
PM and CM have no pardoning power at all.

PYQ-POL-APK-51931E.lead: President's rule was imposed in Andhra Pradesh in January 1973.

Jalagam Vengala Rao became CM when it ended.

PYQ-POL-APK-519324.lead: All three statements correctly describe Centre-State administrative relations.

PYQ-POL-APK-606966.lead: A Bill becomes an Act after both Houses pass it and the President assents.

PYQ-POL-APK-71CDB5.lead: The President's office is created by the Constitution itself (Article 52).

PYQ-POL-APK-A3045C.lead: Under Article 80, the President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha.

PYQ-POL-APK-B47923.lead: The Governor sends the report on constitutional failure to the President.
points: Article 356 lets the President act on the Governor's report or otherwise.

PYQ-POL-APK-B47923.also: S.R. Bommai case (1994): President's rule is subject to judicial review.

PYQ-POL-APK-B57028.lead: Article 61: impeachment charges can be started in either House of Parliament.

PYQ-POL-APK-B6FA3A.lead: Article 65: the Vice President acts as President during a vacancy.

PYQ-POL-APK-BACE53.lead: CJI M. Hidayatullah acted as President in 1969.

Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed was an elected President, not a CJI.

PYQ-POL-APK-C3FE68.lead: President's rule can be extended up to a maximum of three years.

PYQ-POL-APK-C4CC03.lead: Article 61: impeachment ground is only 'violation of the Constitution'.

PYQ-POL-APK-DA7524.lead: Electoral college: elected MPs, elected MLAs of states, Delhi and Puducherry.

Members of Legislative Councils do not vote.

PYQ-POL-APK-DA7524.also: Article 54 lists the electoral college; Article 55 the voting method.

PYQ-POL-APK-E88DC3.lead: Article 103: President must get EC opinion and act accordingly.

PYQ-POL-APK-FE8807.lead: K.K. Venugopal is known as Attorney General of India (Article 76).

PYQ-POL-D54EB893C173.lead: Article 57: a President is eligible for re-election any number of times.

PYQ-POL-E44F3D880178.lead: An ordinance can last at most six months and six weeks.

PYQ-POL-E8D6CB50FE94.lead: Article 57: no limit on re-election of the President.
points: A former or sitting President can stand again any number of times.
Rajendra Prasad is the only one elected twice.

PYQ-POL-EC48099266C1.lead: Only elected members of Parliament and of state and UT assemblies vote.
points: Voters: elected MPs of both Houses, and elected MLAs of states, Delhi and Puducherry.
Nominated members and Legislative Council members do not vote.

PYQ-POL-ED121CA014F5.lead: Article 111: President can return a non-Money Bill once for reconsideration.

PYQ-POL-EEE6118723DB.lead: Only the President can pardon a death sentence; the Governor cannot.

PYQ-POL-FB80B6E61897.lead: Article 77: all executive action of GoI is taken in the President's name.

points: The Prime Minister, Attorney General and Vice-President have no pardoning power.

PYQ-POL-WEB-6E7256.lead: Article 56 fixes the President's five-year term.

PYQ-POL-WEB-77C1B2.lead: Art 123 allows ordinances unless both Houses are in session.

PYQ-POL-WEB-828124.lead: Art 123 gives the President power to issue ordinances.

Governors issue ordinances for States under Article 213.

PYQ-POL-WEB-8CD7DA.lead: The President is the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces (Art 53(2)).

PYQ-POL-WEB-9B7669.lead: Presidential system rests on one leader; parliamentary on collective leadership.

PYQ-POL-WEB-9EB4D2.lead: Art 61: impeachment charges can begin in either House of Parliament.

PYQ-POL-081155950B58.lead: Indian judicial review is narrower than the American one.
points: India follows 'procedure established by law'; the USA follows 'due process of law'.
High Courts also have judicial review power, not only the Supreme Court.

Article 134 deals with criminal appeals to the Supreme Court, not judicial review.

PYQ-POL-121EB5644B06.lead: Both Supreme Court and High Courts can strike down unconstitutional laws.

PYQ-POL-2B489090B8F2.lead: Judicial review means checking if laws and executive orders are constitutional.

Reviewing its own judgement is 'review' under Article 137, a different power.

PYQ-POL-BA4E93E88A7D.lead: Judicial activism is courts actively stepping in to protect public interest.

Setting aside elections is a normal judicial function, not activism.

PYQ-POL-0DB21DF7CD3C.lead: PIL is the main tool of judicial activism.
points: PIL relaxed the rule of 'locus standi', letting anyone approach the court for others.

PYQ-POL-2F4A7E41090F.lead: India's first reported PIL was Hussainara Khatoon case, 1979.

PYQ-POL-WEB-1524E4.lead: Justice P.N. Bhagwati pioneered PIL in India.

PYQ-POL-WEB-1524E4.also: He was Chief Justice of India in 1985–86.

PYQ-POL-WEB-3008C1.lead: PIL originated in the USA in the 1960s.
points: It was used there for civil rights and poor people's legal causes.
India adopted it in the late 1970s.

PYQ-POL-WEB-3C2D8C.lead: PIL is linked with judicial activism.
